Ha - I don't know either. Nobody knows.

But let's make this interesting.

Claim: by the end of 2030, real median weekly earnings of US professional workers will be at least 10% below today’s level.

This formalizes a fragment from October 2026: that the return on a lot of labor is going to zero. 

Brady’s objection was fair: “I don’t think that’s going to happen” invites “well, what do you think is going to happen?” So here’s a claim that can lose. Not zero, but a decline that this series has never recorded in its 26-year history.

Probability: 0.85

Resolves YES if the Q4 2030 value of FRED series LEU0254530200Q (BLS, median usual weekly nominal earnings, full-time wage and salary workers, professional and related occupations, 16 and over), divided by the Q4 2030 average of CPIAUCSL (October, November, December 2030), is at or below 4.300. That threshold is 90% of the latest published reading, Q2 2026: $1,591 / 332.99 = 4.778. If Q4 2030 hasn’t posted by the resolution date, I’ll use the latest 2030 quarter available with its matching three-month CPI average and say so. Values as published on FRED on the resolution date. Resolves NO otherwise.

For scale: at 2.5% annual inflation, YES means nominal median professional earnings are flat or lower in late 2030 than they are today.

The resolution will be a new version of this item, with evidence. Any revision before then will say what changed and why.

Second live test of the prediction-journal shape from blygger-spec#10: https://github.com/blygger/blygger-spec/issues/10


```
{
  "claim": "Real median weekly earnings of US professional workers (LEU0254530200Q / CPIAUCSL) are at least 10% below the Q2 2026 level by Q4 2030",
  "probability": 0.85,
  "resolves_by": "2031-03-31",
  "criteria": "LEU0254530200Q (Q4 2030) / mean(CPIAUCSL Oct–Dec 2030) <= 4.300; baseline Q2 2026 = 1591 / 332.99 = 4.778; fallback latest 2030 quarter with matching 3-month CPI mean; values as published on FRED at resolution",
  "provenance": "https://caseyjr.org/blyg/t/02ahmfdtqb83dwmx9xkqr1rcxj/",
  "discussion": "https://github.com/blygger/blygger-spec/issues/10"
}
```

Stubbing: This is likely an unpopular thought in the thicket, but the return on a lot of labor is going to zero dunno what counts are labor...

This is likely an unpopular thought in the thicket, but the return on a lot of labor is going to zero

dunno what counts are labor... most my life is oriented around fun. A lot of it is difficult fun, and needs work—heck, even labor—but still fun.

I'm thinking of paid labor (jobs), particularly for cognitive tasks.

I suspect this isn't precisely true but only because because it's too neat. That's my whole counterpoint, which I know is a weak counterpoint. A good rule of history is that the big trends turn out surprising. 

The trouble with having a dispute over this looking forward though is that you can't really say more than: "I don't think that's going to happen," because the natural rejoinder is, "Well, what do you think is going to happen?"

My only answer to that is: "I don't know! It's going to be surprising!" 

And that's not a very compelling argument, I grant you.
